name: Sicel

ancestors.notes: The prevalent modern view treats Sicel as an Italic language, but the scarcity of sources makes a definitive conclusion impossible (Wikipedia: Sicel language; Weiss 2022). Low weight reflects that classification uncertainty.
Attested only through a Greek (likely Euboic-Chalkidic) alphabet borrowed under contact with Greek colonists in eastern Sicily (Tribulato 2012).

notes: Stub: no citable grapheme-to-IPA inventory. Extinct, definitely Indo-European language of ancient eastern Sicily, attested in fewer than thirty inscriptions (only ~6 considered intelligibly Sicel) plus ~25 glosses in ancient authors, written in the Greek alphabet. No published phonological inventory (grapheme-by-grapheme sound values) is sourceable from the extremely limited corpus; the literature (Hartmann 2017, Weiss 2022, Tribulato 2012) discusses individual sound-law arguments (e.g. reflexes of PIE voiced aspirates) from isolated forms, not a systematic orthography-to-phoneme table, so graphemes is left empty rather than fabricated from Greek-alphabet defaults.
